newsitem.title: LATVIA: LATVIA-PARTIES PICK KRASTS AS NEW PRIME MINISTER.
newsitem.headline: LATVIA-PARTIES PICK KRASTS AS NEW PRIME MINISTER.

text.p: Latvia's three largest political parties on Monday decided to nominate Economy Minister Guntar Krasts as new prime minister, officials said.

"Of all candidates he (Krasts) was the best," said Indulis Berzinsh, leading member of second-largest party, Latvia's Way. Krasts will replace outgoing premier Andris Shkele, forced to resign last week after a string of ministerial resignations amid corruption scandals.
Shkele was also involved in increasingly bitter rows with the seven parties that formed his government, making his position untenable.
Krasts, 39, is a member of third-largest party in parliament, nationalist group For Fatherland and Freedom.
He is seen as something of a technocrat and is untested as a political leader. He has been economy minister since late 1995, when Shkele first came to power.
Shkele, a no-nonsense businessman, was credited with giving a big push to the reforms Latvia launched after quitting the former Soviet Union in 1991.
His main achievements were seen as speeding privatisation and getting state finances in order by forcing through balanced budgets.
